newsitem.title: USA: Arco has lower earnings due to contract expirations.
newsitem.headline: Arco has lower earnings due to contract expirations.

text.p: Arco Chemical Co. reported lower first-quarter earnings Monday, hurt by the expiration of a number of fixed margin contracts for an additive that makes gasoline burn cleaner.
The company said its earnings for the quarter declined to $48 million, or 50 cents a share, from $106 million, or $1.10 a share, in the similar quarter in 1996.
Revenues rose to $1 billion from $982 million a year earlier, helped by strong sales volumes in the company's propylene oxide derivatives businesses.

With the expiration of the fixed-price contracts for the gasoline additive, methyl tertiary butyl ether, it is considered likely that the price will fall further because world-wide production capacity has gone up.
Alan Hirsig, president and chief executive officer, said the development was expected, adding "we had anticipated that 1997 would be a challenging year for Arco Chemical."
At the same time, Hirsig said that during the first quarter high raw material costs, coupled with weak product pricing, compressed margins in virtually all of the company's businesses.

To mitigate profit fluctuations and give shareholders long-term value, Arco Chemical has taken several steps, he said, including tying executives' compensation to profit. In addition, executives will be required to own company stock at levels of one to four times base salary, he said.
The company is also implementing a broad programme designed to increase efficiency and to achieve a very substantial reduction in structural costs, he said.
Arco's stock was unchanged at $42 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
